samples.summary: New /insert and /move endpoints accept index/count up to 1,000,000, which drives axis-ID generation past the 36^4 (~1.68M) ID space and into a non-terminating retry loop — a permanent event-loop hang of the backend from one small authenticated POST
samples.evidence:
Attack: with any workspace-member session or a write-scoped API key (WorkspaceScopeGuard only requires membership; there is no viewer role — yorkie-auth.controller.ts:178 confirms membership = read+write), POST /api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/documents/{doc}/tabs/{tab}/insert with body {"axis":"row","index":1,"count":1000000} twice (or once with {"index":1000000,"count":1000000}).

Chain: parseCount (worksheet-structure.ts:143-156) and parseIndex (:123) bound both fields only by axisLimit(axis) = MaxRows = 1_000_000 for rows. The controller then calls applyWorksheetShift -> insertWorksheetAxis (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-axis.ts:25), which calls ensureAxisLength(index-1) and then mints `count` fresh IDs, each via createWorksheetAxisId (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:89). That generator draws a 4-char id from a 36-char alphabet (AXIS_ID_LENGTH = 4 -> 36^4 = 1,679,616 distinct ids per prefix) inside `for(;;)` and retries whenever the id is already in `existing`, with no attempt limit. Once rowOrder holds more than ~1.68M ids the loop can never terminate: it is a synchronous infinite loop inside doc.update, inside the request handler, so the whole Node process (all tenants, all routes) is wedged until it is killed — no timeout can interrupt it.

Even short of exhaustion, the repo's own design note measures this exact code path at ~7 minutes of blocking Yorkie pushes for 1M axis ids in a single doc.update (docs/design/sheets/axis-id-selection.md:181-186, which explicitly lists insertWorksheetAxis / moveWorksheetAxis as reproducing the freeze), and yorkie.service.ts:57-60 then pushes the resulting changepack. The neighbouring clear endpoint in this same file caps work deliberately at MaxClearedCells = 1e6 (~0.5s, worksheet-structure.ts:14-30); the new axis validator reuses the raw grid bound instead, which is precisely the pathological value. The editor path cannot reach these magnitudes (selection-driven extension is capped by MaxAxisCoverage = 10000, packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:166), so this is a bound that only the new REST surface removes. The global throttler (app.module.ts:101, 120 req/min per caller) does not help — one request suffices.

samples.summary: Nothing caps the resulting rowOrder/colOrder length, so repeated /insert calls grow a document's axis arrays without limit (past the 1e6 grid bound), giving unbounded per-request CRDT/storage amplification
samples.evidence: parseAxisShift validates each request in isolation (index <= 1e6, count <= 1e6) but neither the validator nor insertWorksheetAxis (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-axis.ts:25-45) checks order.length + count against MaxRows/MaxColumns. An attacker with write access repeats POST .../insert {"axis":"row","index":1,"count":1000000}; each call appends up to 1e6 CRDT array elements to root.sheets[tab].rowOrder and each is synced to the Yorkie server (yorkie.service.ts:59), so a handful of ~50-byte requests inflates one document's CRDT to millions of nodes — memory/storage exhaustion for the backend process that later attaches the document and for the Yorkie server, and it is also what walks the document into the id-space exhaustion hang described in the other finding. Searched for an existing cap: grepped rowOrder.length/colOrder.length/MaxAxisCoverage across packages (only the frontend store's ensureAxisOrder and the engine's selection cap, neither on this path), grepped MaxRows|MaxColumns|1000000|18278 across packages/backend/src (only per-request bounds in worksheet-settings.ts and worksheet-structure.ts), and read insertWorksheetAxis/ensureAxisLength and the controller's applyShift in full.

samples.summary: The unvalidated `tabId` path segment is used directly as a property key (`root.sheets?.[tabId]`), and the new insert/delete/move handlers now write through whatever object that lookup returns — a possible `__proto__`/`constructor` prototype-pollution vector
samples.evidence: worksheetOrThrow (line 68) does `root.sheets?.[tabId]` with tabId taken verbatim from the URL and only rejects falsy results; a request to .../tabs/__proto__/insert supplies `__proto__` as the key. On a plain object that lookup yields Object.prototype (truthy), and unlike the pre-existing clear handler the new handlers hand the result to applyWorksheetShift/applyWorksheetMove, which assign rowOrder/colOrder/cells onto it — i.e. writes onto the prototype of every object in the process. I could not confirm exploitability: in production `root` is a Yorkie CRDT proxy and the SDK is not vendored in this checkout (no node_modules/@yorkie-js/sdk), so I could not verify whether its get trap returns undefined for `__proto__` rather than falling through. Note the codebase elsewhere treats exactly this as a threat and validates keys before use (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:117 and its `__proto__` regression test), which the tab lookup does not. The pattern predates this diff (clear/dimensions controllers) but the diff adds the first write-through-the-result paths.
